title: Recipe 25 — VS Code and JetBrains (the editor surfaces, from the CLI side)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Two plugins, one JSON Schema, and every command they expose shells out to the CLI you already have. Nothing in the editor is privileged.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed starter and the recipe are never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env into this one terminal — the same environment the editor's Run Spec command inherits.

groups.title: Beat 1 · the spec the editor lints

beats.label: Type recipe 01's harness
beats.cue: “The plainest spec there is — this is what the language id crewhaus-spec attaches to, and what the schema's target union validates.”

beats.label: Lint it from the shell
beats.cue: “Same verdict the editor's squiggles carry. The plugins do not hold a second opinion.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “Autocomplete is a nicety; this is the contract. Every target shape in the schema union has to lower to one of these.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target cli

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN with no key.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: “Go to Definition on a sub-agent gets you a markdown file; Open Trace gets you a webview. Neither one hides this.”

beats.label: Blank the workspace settings
beats.cue: “Three settings is the whole VS Code surface: where the CLI is, where Studio is, and which files the schema applies to.”

beats.label: Type the recipe's settings.json
beats.cue: “cliPath is why the extension ships no bundled binary. studioUrl is why Open Trace works against a cluster-hosted Studio.”

beats.label: Prove it is valid JSON
beats.cue: “A malformed settings.json is the most common reason a plugin looks broken — so check it before the editor does.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const s = await Bun.file(".vscode/settings.json").json(); console.log("settings.json: valid —", Object.keys(s).join(", "))'

beats.label: Blank the sub-agent definition
beats.cue: “Hovering a sub-agent name resolves exactly one path: dot-crewhaus, sub-agents, name dot md. That resolver is the hover card.”

beats.label: Type the recipe's sub-agent
beats.cue: “Frontmatter plus a body. The hover renders the frontmatter; the body is what the sub-agent actually runs on.”

beats.label: Print what the hover would render
beats.cue: “Name, description, tool list — and nothing else, because the body is too long for a hover. That is the whole card.”

verify.note: prints name: code-reviewer / description: … / tools: [read, grep, bash] — the three fields resolveSubAgentDefinition surfaces

beats.label: Open the definition itself
beats.cue: “And this is where Go to Definition lands. The resolver refuses any name carrying a slash, a dot-dot, or a null byte — same rule as the runtime.”

groups.title: Beat 5 · run it without leaving the editor

beats.label: Run the spec
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Right-click, CrewHaus: Run Spec. It opens a terminal in the spec's directory and runs this — verbatim.”

verify.note: interactive REPL; needs Anthropic credentials. This is what crewhaus.runSpec shells out to via crewhaus.cliPath.

beats.label: Exit the REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] “exit” returns to the shell, and the terminal panel keeps the transcript.

groups.title: One more thing · what CI actually proves

beats.label: Run the JetBrains smoke
beats.cue: [manual] “The Gradle build is gated on JBR_BIN so the unit tier stays fast — and the smoke proves that gate, both ways.”

verify.note: needs the sibling factory workspace: this smoke imports a @crewhaus package that is not published and not declared by demos, so a bare `bun install --frozen-lockfile` checkout (CI) cannot resolve it. Passes on a dev machine with the workspace linked.

beats.label: Run the Studio playground smoke
beats.cue: [manual] “The trace webview both plugins open is Studio — this smokes Studio against a synthetic spec, quota rejection and all.”

verify.note: needs the sibling factory workspace: this smoke imports a @crewhaus package that is not published and not declared by demos, so a bare `bun install --frozen-lockfile` checkout (CI) cannot resolve it. Passes on a dev machine with the workspace linked.

beats.label: The VS Code extension smoke
beats.cue: [manual] “Type-checks the extension and packages a vsix — that one needs a utilities checkout beside this repo, so run it there.”

verify.note: NOT driven offline: it imports @crewhaus/vscode-extension/run-spec, which lives in the sibling crewhaus/utilities repo. The drivers CI clones only factory, and the tsconfig paths mapping cannot resolve that package's subpath export, so it fails with 'Cannot find module'. Needs a human with a utilities checkout.
